name: Ephod The
overview: The ephod, as described in Exodus 28, was a sacred garment worn by the high priest, symbolizing his role in bearing the names of the twelve tribes of Israel before the LORD. It was intricately made with onyx stones engraved with the tribes' names, set in gold and fastened on the shoulders as a memorial (Exodus 28:9-12). The ephod was closely associated with the breastplate of judgment, connected by gold rings and chains, and was crafted from fine materials including gold, blue, purple, and scarlet, reflecting its holy significance (Exodus 28:25-26). This garment not only identified the high priest's office but also served as a tangible reminder of Israel's covenant relationship with God.
